title: Study
description: One study: a book of the Bible, or a topical or thematic study across passages. Enforcement lives in tools/validate.mjs, which gives better error messages than a schema can; this file exists for editor autocomplete and as documentation.

id.description: Stable identifier. Notes and progress are saved under bsg:<id>: in the reader's browser, so NEVER change it once published.

kind.description: book = one book of the Bible, worked through in order. topic = a theme traced across passages from many books.

status.description: Only published studies are built into the site. Drafts build with: node tools/build.mjs --drafts

title.description: Short name, e.g. Romans, or The Fruit of the Spirit

pageTitle.description: The h1. Defaults to title plus Study Guide.

docTitle.description: Browser tab and search result title.

metaDescription.description: One or two sentences for search results and link previews.

progressOpening.description: The message shown beside the progress bar at 0%.

canon.description: For kind book: where it sits in Scripture. Used for ordering on the home page.

group.description: e.g. Pauline epistles, Torah, Major prophets, Gospels

category.description: e.g. Christian living, Doctrine, Prayer, Character

anchorBooks.description: The books this study draws on most.

sources.description: Where the historical and background claims come from. Study guides that assert history should say who says so.

units.description: The tabs of the study, in order. Conventionally overview, background, study1..studyN, summary.

id.description: Stable unit id, also the URL hash (#study3). Never change it once published.

title.description: The h2 at the top of the unit.

passages.description: The passage or passages this unit works through, e.g. ["Romans 1-3"] or, for a topical study, several references from different books.

block.description: One card in a unit. The type decides how it looks and what it means.

oneOf.title: themes / prose / context / warning / application / highlight / observe / wordstudy / hardquestion

type.description: themes: key themes. prose: plain teaching. context: historical background. warning: a caution or a false teaching. application: living it out. highlight: a featured callout. observe: observation prompts to do before being told what it means. wordstudy: a Greek or Hebrew term. hardquestion: an honest difficulty in the text, named rather than avoided.

ref.description: e.g. Galatians 3:13-14. The text is filled in at build time from content/scripture, never typed here.

crossRefs.description: References the reader can open and read in place.

text.description: Optional. Left out, the passage text is used.

audience.description: e.g. Personal, Group Discussion, For leaders

id.description: Stable id. The reader's saved notes are keyed to it, so never change it once published.
Stable id. Saved ticks are keyed to it, so never change it once published.

node.description: One piece of content inside a card. Exactly one key. Inline markup allowed in text: strong, em, a.

h4.description: A small sub-heading inside the card.
